http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in hypermorphosis relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Peramorphosis that is produced by a delay in the offset of development.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in synology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Xenology that results, not from the transfer of a gene between two species, but from a hybridization of two species.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in isoorthology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Orthology that involves functional equivalent genes with retention of the ancestral function.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in tandem paralogy relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Paralogy that is characterized by duplication of adjacent sequences on a chromosome segment.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in latent homology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Parallelism that involves morphologically very similar structures, occurring only within some members of a taxon and absent in the common ancestor (which possessed the developmental basis to develop this character).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in syngeny relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Homocracy that involves recognizably corresponding characters that occurs in two or more taxa, or as a repeated unit within an individual.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in apparent orthology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Between-species paralogy that involves single copy paralogs resulting from reciprocal gene loss.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in pseudoparalogy relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Xenology that involves genes that ended up in a given genome as a result of a combination of vertical inheritance and horizontal gene transfer.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in equivalogy relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Historical homology that involves functional equivalent genes with retention of the ancestral function.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in interology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Historical homology that involves orthologous pairs of interacting molecules in different organisms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in functional equivalence relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Similarity that is characterized by interchangeability in function.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in iterative homology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Biological homology that involves parts of the same organism.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in paraxenology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Xenology that is characterized by multiple horizontal transfer events, resulting in the presence of two or more copies of the foreign gene in the host genome.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in plerology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Paralogy that is characterized by extra similarity between paralogous sequences resulting from concerted evolution.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in homotopy relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Structural homology that involves structures with the same or similar relative positions.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in homeosis relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Biological homology that involves an ectopic structure and the normally positioned structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in homoeology relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Synology that results from allopolyploidy.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in paramorphism relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Iterative homology that involves two structures, one of which originated as a duplicate of the other and co-opted the expression of patterning genes of the ancestral structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.label: in regulogy relationship with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_HOM000.definition: Historical homology that involves orthologous pairs of transcription factors and downstream regulated genes in different organisms.
